issue: Honorific violation: 할아버지는 나이가 많아요 — about one's own grandfather natives must say 연세가 많으세요 (honorific noun 연세 + -세요). The deck itself honors grandparents two cards away (계세요 ko-0940, 드세요 ko-0942), so plain 나이가 많아요 is an internal contradiction. Engine can't derive 많으세요, so swap to a non-honored subject.

fix.english: Our dog is old.
fix.grammar: 나이가 많아요 (nai-ga manayo) = 'is old' — literally 'age is many'.

issue: Honorific mismatch: 이분 (honorific 'this person') paired with plain copula 예요 about one's own mother. The deck's own ko-0019 models the correct pattern (이분은 박 선생님이세요) — once you elevate with 이분, the predicate must be -세요. Dict already lexicalizes 선생님이세요, so 어머니세요 follows the same engine-safe pattern.

fix.english: This is my mother.
fix.grammar: 이분 takes polite 세요: 어머니세요 (eomeoni-seyo = is my mother); the plain form is 어머니예요.

어머니세요.en: is (my) mother (polite -세요 copula, pairs with 이분/그분)

issue: Gloss/target modality mismatch: 다른 사이즈로 바꿔요? cannot mean 'Can I exchange...?' — plain -어요? asks a factual question ('are you exchanging?'), not permission/ability. The natural customer line uses V-어 주세요, already taught at ko-0828 (깎아 주세요) and ko-0893.

fix.target: 이 바지를 다른 사이즈로 바꿔 주세요.
fix.english: Please exchange these pants for a different size.
fix.grammar: V-어 주세요 = 'please do it for me': 바꿔 주세요 (bakkwo juseyo = please exchange it).

issue: Missing subject honorific: plain 살아요 about one's own parents; natives say 사세요 (precedent: ko-0137 audit fix). Engine can't derive -세요 forms, but the suppletive honorific 계세요 is already in the deck/dict and gives a natural equivalent. This also makes 계세요's first family use tipped here.

fix.english: My parents are in Seoul.
fix.grammar: 계세요 (gyeseyo) = honorific 'are (there)' for parents and elders; the plain form is 있어요 (isseoyo).

issue: Missing subject honorific: 아버지는 ... 일해요 — plain verb about one's own father; natives say 일하세요. Engine can't derive -세요, so per the ko-0137 precedent swap to a sibling subject, which takes plain forms naturally.

fix.english: My older brother works at a company.

issue: Missing subject honorific: 어머니는 요리를 잘해요 — the exact defect class the ko-0137 audit fixed (plain verb about one's own mother; natives say 잘하세요). Swap to spouse, who takes plain forms; keeps the 잘 + verb teaching point intact.

fix.english: My husband cooks well.
fix.grammar: 잘 + verb = do well: 요리를 잘해요 (yori-reul jalhaeyo = cooks well).

issue: Missing subject honorific: 할머니는 마음이 따뜻해요 — plain descriptive about one's own grandmother; natives say 따뜻하세요. Directly inconsistent with the deck honoring the same grandmother with 계세요 (ko-0939) and 드세요 (ko-0941). Engine can't derive -세요; swap subject.

fix.english: My friend is warm-hearted.
fix.grammar: 마음이 따뜻해요 (maeum-i ttatteuthaeyo) = warm-hearted — 마음 = heart, mind.

issue: Honorific mismatch: 그분 (respectful 'that person') with plain 나이가 많아요. Elevating with 그분 requires honorific predicates (연세가 많으세요) — cf. deck's own 이분은 박 선생님이세요 (ko-0019). Engine-safe fix reuses taught suppletive 계세요 and keeps the 그분 teaching point.

fix.english: Where is that person right now?
fix.grammar: 그분 (geubun) = respectful 'that person' — pair it with polite verbs like 계세요 (gyeseyo).

issue: Missing subject honorific: 엄마가 케이크를 만들었어요 — plain past about one's own mom; careful speech uses 만드셨어요, which the engine can't derive. Swap subject per ko-0137 precedent.

fix.english: My friend made the cake.

issue: Register mix: 과 is the written/formal connector; deck canon for speech is 랑/이랑 (랑 tipped on ko-0801 immediately before, 이랑 already modeled at ko-0384/0469). Precedent: ko-0165 audit replaced 와 with 랑. The tip even teaches the formal particle as the default spoken 'and'. Same-class offenders outside this fix: ko-0654, ko-1081, ko-1129, ko-1168, ko-1279, ko-1294 (other slices).

fix.english: I buy fruit and vegetables at the market.
fix.grammar: 이랑 (irang) = 'and/with' after a consonant: 과일이랑 야채 (gwail-irang yachae); after a vowel it's 랑 (rang).

issue: Register mix: 라면과 김밥 — written/formal 과 in a spoken convenience-store sentence; deck canon is 이랑 (see ko-0802 fix, ko-0165 precedent).

fix.english: I buy ramyeon and gimbap at the convenience store.

issue: Register mix: 치마와 바지 — formal 와 for spoken 'and'; deck canon is 랑 after vowels (tipped ko-0801).

fix.english: I'm buying a skirt and pants.

issue: Register mix plus tip conflict: 부모님과 with a tip teaching 과/와 = 'with' — but the deck already models the spoken form 부모님이랑 (ko-0469) and fixed 누구와 to 누구랑 (ko-0165 audit). Teaching 과/와 as the spoken comitative contradicts deck canon; dict even has a 부모님이랑 entry.

fix.english: I live with my parents.
fix.grammar: 이랑 (irang) = 'with' after a consonant: 부모님이랑 (bumonim-irang = with my parents).

issue: Register mix: 여동생과 — formal comitative in a spoken sentence; deck canon is 이랑.

fix.english: I talk on the phone with my younger sister every day.

issue: Register mix: 형과 저는 — formal 과 in speech; deck canon is 이랑. (Speaker-gender note: 형 implies a male speaker; rule gets tipped at the ko-0953 fix.)

fix.english: My older brother and I look really alike.

issue: Register mix: 저와 — formal 와 in a spoken sentence; canon is 저랑 (cf. 누구랑, ko-0165 precedent).

fix.english: My cousin is the same age as me.
fix.grammar: 같아요 (gatayo) = is the same: 나이가 같아요 (nai-ga gatayo = same age).

issue: Speaker-gender ambiguity: first FIRST-PERSON use of 형 (ko-0934 was third-person Junho), untipped, one card after a female-speaker card (ko-0952 우리 언니) — the deck silently flips speaker gender between adjacent 'my older brother/sister' cards. First first-person use of each gendered term needs its own tip.

fix.english: My older brother is still a student.
fix.grammar: 형 (hyeong) = a man's older brother, so this speaker is male. Women say 오빠 (oppa).

issue: Speaker-gender ambiguity: first first-person use of 오빠 (ko-0935 was third-person Sujin), untipped, directly after a male-speaker 형 card — 'my older brother' glosses to two different words on adjacent cards with no explanation.

fix.english: My older brother got married last week.
fix.grammar: 오빠 (oppa) = a woman's older brother, so this speaker is female. Men say 형 (hyeong).

issue: Speaker-gender ambiguity: first first-person use of 누나 (ko-0933 was third-person Minsu), untipped; the surrounding cards alternate female (언니/오빠) and male (형/누나) speakers card-by-card.

fix.english: My older sister works at a hospital.
fix.grammar: 누나 (nuna) = a man's older sister, so this speaker is male. Women say 언니 (eonni).

issue: Tip gap on honorific: ko-0941 tips 드세요 as imperative 'please eat', then this card uses the identical form declaratively ('grandfather is eating') with no tip — as taught, the learner reads 'Grandfather, please eat breakfast'. The dual statement/request reading of -세요 must be tipped here.

fix.english: My grandfather is eating breakfast.
fix.grammar: 드세요 also STATES what an elder does: 아침을 드세요 (achim-eul deuseyo = he's eating breakfast).

issue: Register mismatch: 이분 (honorific 'this person') to introduce one's OWN friend — the exact defect the ko-0018 audit fixed (friends/equals take neutral 이쪽). Repeating the ko-0018 fix verbatim would duplicate that sentence, so pivot to spouse; this also debuts 이쪽 with a tip before ko-1029 reinforces it.

fix.english: This is my husband.
fix.grammar: 이쪽은 (ijjog-eun) = 'this side is…' — the polite-neutral way to introduce family and friends.

issue: Gloss/target mismatch: plain present 소개해요 is not performative — 'Let me introduce...' is 소개할게요, which the engine can't derive. Keep a plain declarative and gloss it honestly by adding a recipient.

fix.english: I'm introducing my friend to my family.

issue: Gloss/target mismatch: same performative-'Let me introduce' problem as ko-1026; plain 소개해요 needs a plain declarative gloss and a recipient to sound natural.

fix.english: Today I'm introducing my father to my friend.

issue: Unnatural question word: sizes are numbers, so Koreans ask 몇 사이즈 (or 사이즈가 어떻게 돼요?), not 무슨 사이즈. 몇 is already taught (ko-0183), so no ordering problem.

fix.english: What size do you wear?
fix.grammar: 몇 (myeot) asks 'what number': 몇 사이즈 (myeot saijeu = what size).

issue: Calque: 세일에서 샀어요 treats the sale as a place ('at the sale') — English-shaped. Natives say 세일 때 샀어요 (during the sale). 때 already taught (ko-0798 휴가 때) and in dict.

fix.english: I bought that watch on sale.
fix.grammar: 때 (ttae) = 'the time of': 세일 때 (seil ttae = during the sale).

issue: Calque: 세일에서 — same 'at the sale' Anglicism as ko-0912; use 세일 때.

fix.english: I'll buy sneakers in the sale.

issue: Missing indirect honorific: 아버지는 머리가 짧아요 — careful speech about one's father's features uses 짧으세요 (indirect honorific); engine can't derive it, so swap to a sibling. Keeps the 머리 = head/hair teaching point.

fix.english: My younger brother has short hair.
fix.grammar: 머리 (meori) = head AND hair: 머리가 짧아요 (meori-ga jjalbayo = has short hair).

issue: Missing indirect honorific: 어머니는 머리가 길어요 → 길으세요/기세요 territory in careful speech; swap to sibling like ko-0963.

fix.english: My younger sister has long hair.

issue: Missing indirect honorific: 아빠는 목소리가 커요 — careful speech uses 크세요 about one's father; engine-safe swap to a non-honored family member.

fix.english: My son has a loud voice.

issue: Gloss calque: 'the mart' is Konglish, not natural English — 마트 is a (big-box) supermarket. Same gloss defect on ko-0808, ko-0813, ko-0916 (fixed below) and ko-0342 (outside this slice).

fix.english: The supermarket is close to my house.

issue: Gloss calque: 'the mart' (see ko-0803).

fix.english: The market is cheaper than the supermarket.
fix.grammar: N보다 (boda) = 'than N': 마트보다 싸요 (mateu-boda ssayo = cheaper than the supermarket).

issue: Gloss calque: 'the mart' (see ko-0803).

fix.english: The supermarket closes at ten at night.

issue: Gloss calque: 'the mart' (see ko-0803).

fix.english: Tomorrow I'll go to the supermarket.
fix.grammar: Future = stem + ㄹ 거예요: 가다 → 갈 거예요 (gal geoyeyo = will go).
